title: Newton's Three Laws of Motion
text: First law: an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net force. Second law: force = mass x acceleration (F=ma). Third law: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

title: Speed, Velocity, and Acceleration
text: Speed = distance/time. Velocity is speed with direction. Acceleration = change in velocity / time taken, measured in m/s^2.

title: Ohm's Law
text: Voltage = Current x Resistance (V=IR). This describes the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.

title: Conservation of Energy
text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another (e.g. kinetic to potential). Total energy in a closed system remains constant.

title: Kinetic and Potential Energy
text: Kinetic energy = 1/2 x mass x velocity^2. Gravitational potential energy = mass x gravity x height (PE = mgh).

title: Wave Basics
text: Wave speed = frequency x wavelength (v = fλ). Frequency is measured in Hertz (cycles per second); wavelength is the distance between two successive peaks.

title: Density
text: Density = mass / volume, commonly measured in kg/m^3 or g/cm^3. Objects denser than a fluid sink; less dense objects float.
